properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued August 6 at 11:44AM EDT until August 6 at 12:15PM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Gulf Waters from East Cape Sable to Chokoloskee 20 to 60 nm out and
beyond 5 fathoms...
Gulf of America including Dry Tortugas and Rebecca Shoal Channel...

* Until 1215 PM EDT.

* At 1144 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 8 nm north of New
Ground Rocks Light, moving northwest at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 6 at 8:07AM MST until August 6 at 1:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
FFWTWC

The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
North Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 100 PM MST.

* At 807 AM MST, local law enforcement reported cars stuck along
Brawley Wash and the Brawley Wash stream gauge near Three Points is
currently at 12.59 feet. Brawley Wash at Milewide Road is
forecasted to reach 4.59 feet by 10 AM. This is runoff from last
night's thunderstorms and flash flooding is already occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Runoff from thunderstorms
producing flash flooding.

SOURCE...Law enforcement reported and stream gauges.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams,
urban areas, highways, streets and underpasses. Roads and
structures immediately near Brawley Wash may be at risk of
flooding.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Three Points and Picture Rocks.

This includes Route 86 between mile markers 149 and 150.

This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Manville Rd at Brawley Wash.

This includes the following streams and drainages...
Robles Wash, Los, Blanco Wash and Brawley Wash.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain.
Washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 1:00 PM MST. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 1:00 PM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 6 at 8:13AM CDT until August 9 at 7:13AM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
...Forecast flooding changed from Minor to Moderate severity and
increased in duration for the following rivers in Missouri...

Big Creek at Blairstown affecting Henry, Johnson and Cass Counties.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Creek at Blairstown.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, The west bank of the creek begins to flood.
At 23.0 feet, Flooding occurs at the west approach to the N Highway
bridge located 0.2 miles west of Blairstown. Flooding also occurs
across B Highway near Big Creek which is several miles northwest of
Blairstown. At 26.0 feet, Many farm levees along Big Creek are
overtopped. Flooding of rural areas behind the levees occurs.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:00 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 12.4 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 24.1 feet just after midnight tonight.
It will then fall below flood stage Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 1:54PM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 PM AKDT, river gauge reports indicate rises in water
levels from heavy rain across the warned area. Flooding is
ongoing. Between 1.5 and 3 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches are possible.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 12:50pm the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 22.4 feet is expected around 4:00pm
Wednesday.
-The Yentna River at Lake Creek is forecast to go below flood
stage Saturday morning August 8th.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.




- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this morning and continue falling to 3.9 feet Tuesday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 25.8
feet on 06/13/1981.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 6 at 10:30AM CDT until August 6 at 1:30PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
FFWLSX

The National Weather Service in St Louis has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Boone County in central Missouri...

* Until 130 PM CDT.

* At 1030 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Columbia, Ashland, Columbia Regional Airport, Rocheport, Midway,
Easley and McBaine.

This includes the following State Parks...
Rock Bridge State Park and Jewell Cemetery Historic Site.

This includes Interstate 70 in Missouri between exits 115 and 133.
